analysis.title: GS SECTOR SPECIALISTS: Energy, Natural Resources and Utilities Preview: Two Things
key_insights: Adam Wijaya ranks commodity investor interest among US investors: (1) steel, elevated for most of 2026, (2) gold, (3) copper, (4) lithium.
Gold: the debate is whether it touches $3,500 before moving to $5,000. It sits at $3,720 this morning. Concern over cost inflation has eased as diesel has fallen, with rates still a focus.
Copper is a supply story for fundamental investors, but the equities are not trading that way. Growth proxy, AI capex and rates are the three most cited reasons for weakness in desk conversations.
Lithium has moved from consensus long to more negative in a short time, based on the medium-term balance view and price action.

Copper fell 5% yesterday on global growth concerns (BCOM -2%), bearish Chinese demand feedback from the Shanghai CESCO conference, and expectations of US exports, which triggered heavy short-selling on SHFE (Shanghai Futures Exchange).

Adam Gillard's team went to China with a modest copper short based on AI concerns, rates and slower US trade, but did not expect a 5% move. Chinese restocking demand (arb, spreads and premium all at highs) did not prevent it.

Gillard's team says it got wrong how easily trade houses diverted metal to meet the Chinese deficit (CESCO feedback: more than 100k MT diverted for December) and how negative Chinese demand sentiment is.

Bull counter on copper: direct AI copper demand will not drop as capex is committed, scrap stays tight for at least two quarters, mine supply does not rebound in 2027, State Grid tenders are rising into year end, and the US administration will be proactive on trade policy.
Refining: few dedicated investors are positive on the group. The GS Refining Basket is -23% over 1 month against Integrated -9% and E&P -11%.
The market has been relatively immune to recent escalation developments. Today's focus is a headline that Xi, Trump and Putin agree to increase supply of global energy.

Six reasons investors are not buying refiners: gasoline is seasonally weaker with large inventory builds, diesel is the only interesting part of the barrel and has been soft versus expectations, a light turnaround season sets up next year, 4Q revisions likely point lower, sell-side near-term numbers are at a peak, and DOE (Department of Energy inventory) reports have been weak.
Topical refining stocks on the desk: MPC, PARR, DK, VLO.
Charts note mogas (gasoline) climbing and likely to continue, and distillate still below its 5-year average but grinding higher over recent weeks.
